## Overview Follow-up for the B300 NVFP4 AgentX lane of [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4357](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4357) (head `8c8d7789`, key `minimaxm3-fp4-b300-vllm-agentic-mtp`) in `recipes/models/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.yaml`. #63407 moved B300 to this head's curve and #63534 turned it into the `b300_agentx` preset: image `nightly-49cb2bbf`, TP8 at concurrency 1, TP4 at 20 and 24, and TP2 with host KV offload at 24 and 28. Checked against the lane, every preset point matches except one flag, and one comment in the B300 override is no longer accurate. This PR fixes both. ## Claims - `b300_agentx` preset: adds `--enable-chunked-prefill`, which the lane passes at every point. The builder's NVFP4 command does not include it. - B300 override comment: the old comment said the image predates the `--disable-x` aliases. It doesn't. `nightly-49cb2bbf` contains #61479 (`1c4c3197` is an ancestor of `49cb2bbf`), and that image's `vllm/utils/argparse_utils.py` pairs `--enable-x` with `--disable-x` and still accepts `--no-enable-x`. The override keeps the lane's own spelling, `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune`. The comment now also points to the preset instead of the guide for per-point settings. - `meta.date_updated` is now 2026-10-26. ## Validation - `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir /recipes` passes (vllm-project/recipes @ `57e7912`). - I built the full JSON API before and after the change. Only the MiniMax-M3 family changes: `presets/b300_agentx.json` (all five points gain `--enable-chunked-prefill`), plus the embedded preset definition and `date_updated` in `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.json`, `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8.json`, `nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4.json` and `amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4.json`. Builder renders for other GPUs, strategies and variants are unchanged, and so is the B300 builder default. - Every preset point was checked against two sources. The first is the PR-head effective recipe: `agentic.yaml` base plus `override_tp8_c1`, `override_tp4_c20`, `override_tp4_c24`, `override_tp2_c24_dram` and `override_tp2_c28_dram`. The second is the logged `vllm serve` command, the `config.yaml` env and the engine log of run [40022391822](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/40022391822) (all five points). After this change, every serving flag, JSON config and env var matches at all five points. Synthetic rejection is excluded (see below). This covers TP, `--max-num-seqs` (2/30/7/36/36), `--max-num-active-seqs` (6 at c20 only), `--gpu-memory-utilization` (0.95/0.95/0.95/0.92/0.92), capture sizes, the MSA `cutlass` decode backend (TP2 only), the all-reduce backend (`mnnvl` at TP4 c24, `trtllm` elsewhere), and SimpleCPUOffload with `cpu_bytes_to_use` 749000000000 and lazy offload on TP2. The engine logs agree on TP, max-num-seqs, active-seq caps and memory utilization. - Image: digest `sha256:8c1434bf…` carries `ai.vllm.build.commit=49cb2bbf71cfd36ee5aa33d1e184b1cddff55294`, and the run logs show vLLM `0.32.0rc1.dev281+g49cb2bbf7`. - Merged current `main` (`4135590f`). No open PR touches `MiniMax-M3.yaml`. ## Details Excluded as InferenceX-only or cluster-specific: concurrency lists; synthetic acceptance (`rejection_sample_method: synthetic`, `synthetic_acceptance_length: 2.78`; the runbook already covers it); the `KV_OFFLOADING`/`TOTAL_CPU_DRAM_GB` benchmark labels; AIPerf settings; `--served-model-name`, `--host`/`--port`/`--device-ids`; `PYTHONNOUSERSITE`; health-check settings; and the Slurm `time_limit` on the TP2 c28 point. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [ ] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

nodes.body:
## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

This flag is a no-op here. `enable_chunked_prefill` defaults to `None`, and `EngineArgs._set_default_chunked_prefill_and_prefix_caching_args` resolves it to `model_config.is_chunked_prefill_supported`, which is `True` for a decoder-only generate model like MiniMax-M3. I checked `49cb2bbf` (the preset image) and it has the same logic, so the builder's NVFP4 command already runs with chunked prefill on. The log line `Chunked prefill is enabled with max_num_batched_tokens=...` should appear both with and without this flag.

Matching the lane's command line word for word isn't a good reason to add flags that are already the default. It makes the preset look like it differs from the builder when it doesn't, and readers will copy the flag into more recipes, which already have about 40 redundant `--enable-chunked-prefill` occurrences. Could we drop this line? Then the PR's only change is the comment fix. If you'd rather keep the preset identical to the lane, please change the comment to say the flag only mirrors the lane and is the default (no behavior change), not that the builder is missing it.

@@ -550,6 +551,8 @@ presets:
     image: "vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-49cb2bbf71cfd36ee5aa33d1e184b1cddff55294@sha256:8c1434bfee7d7626eef78ef70600434ffba4a1b8813cb1d1c8707ad25f47035e"
     select:
       features: { spec_decoding: eagle3_gqa, text_only: true, thinking_always_on: true }
+    # The lane passes this; the builder's NVFP4 command does not.
+    args: ["--enable-chunked-prefill"]
